 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 24-05-2024 at about 11:45 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in a Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ- 1468, from Kyasamballi village towards Balaganatham village.

At that time, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village,
Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, the driver of said Tata Sumo namely Srinivasulu Reddy drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner got stuck inside the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to PES Hospital, Kuppam, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident she was working as tailor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Ramakuppam Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tata Sumo for the offence punishable under Section 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of Private Car package policy bearing No.0516033123P116864129 in respect of Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and it was valid from 17-03-2024 to 16-03-2025.

Further it is contended that, the driver of the Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1/owner of said vehicle being aware of the same has consciously allowed such person to drive his vehicle and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160442603/
2 Act.

sentences.text: Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1/owner of the Tata Sumo had allowed or permitted his driver to drive the said vehicle in the public place without a valid fitness certificate.
As such, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and had acted in contravention of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988.
Further it is contended that, the said accident has occurred due to contributory negligence of the petitioner.

The accident having occurred at around 11.45 p.m., during the night hours, on a busy road, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village,
Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh.
The petitioner had not taken reasonable care for the safety of herself, as well as the driver of the vehicle.
The act of the petitioner in having taken the risk of engaging the driver in conversion, has led him to jump the vehicle and it has resulted in the accident.

The petitioner is liable for contributory negligence for not less than 75%
and she is "author of her own wrong".
Hence, the compensation if any awarded to the petitioner is to be reduced by 75% having contributed to the accident.
Further, it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA SUMO bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6 . In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Further, she has got examined one more witness namely Dr. S.A.
Somashekara as P.W.2.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., when she was traveling in a Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468, near Green Valley School,
Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, at that time the driver of offending Tata Sumo drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner got stuck inside the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident she was working as tailor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of her oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 and 2(a) are true copy of first information statement and its translated copy, Ex.P.3 and 3(a) are true copy of sketch and its translated copy, Ex.P.4 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.5 is true copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.6 and 7 are discharge summary (total 2), Ex.P.8 to 13 are OPD sheets (total 6), Ex.P.14 are OPD bills (total 9), Ex.P.15 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioner, Ex.P.16 is OPD book and Ex.P.17 is x-ray.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 5, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and dashing the same to the road side tree.
Due to said impact, the petitioner being inmate of said car has sustained grievous injury i.e. right proximal third tibia shaft fracture (segmental).

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.5, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 in the accident, the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place due to the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner, as she had engaged the driver of said vehicle in conversion with him and the same led to the accident.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.
It has neither adduced any evidence, nor it has produced any document to establish the above contentions.

Even,
the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and dashing the same to the road side tree.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160442603/
4 goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to her own negligence or there was any contributory negligence on her part, in the cause of accident.
13.

Further, the Ex.P.3 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the right side of the road, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, due to dashing of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 to the road side tree.
Further, it is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the accident has taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.5 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MJ-1468 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.4 wound certificate, Ex.P.6 and 7 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.8 to 13 OPD sheets (total 6), Ex.P.16 OPD book and Ex.P.17 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in a road traffic accident.
She has suffered right proximal third tibial shaft fracture (segmental).

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and she has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, she has sustained right proximal third tibial shaft fracture (segmental).
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of her Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.15.
As per Ex.P.15, the date of birth of the petitioner is 23-04-2003.
The accident has taken place on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 P.M.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 21 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has sustained right proximal third tibial shaft fracture (segmental) and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 36% to the right lower limb and 18% to the whole body.

The Ex.P.4 wound certificate,
Ex.P.6 and 7 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.8 to 13 OPD sheets (total 6), Ex.P.16 OPD book and Ex.P.17 x-ray also clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injury and for the said injury she has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
He has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 24-05-2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 30-10-2025, which is after lapse of one year and five months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has admitted that, as the petitioner is of tender age the healing process will be faster and the fracture sustained by the petitioner is united before his examination.

Therefore, in such Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160442603/
6 circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

sentences.text: Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
20. The petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, before accident she was working as tailor and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further she has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident she is unable to do her work.
The respondents have specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was working as tailor and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.

21. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 21 years is 18.

Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,98,000 X 12/100 X 18 = Rs.4,27,680/-.
22.
Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, she has produced 9 medical bills, as per Ex.P.14.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.5,118/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,118/- under the head of medical expenses.
23. Pain and sufferings:
In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., right proximal third tibial shaft fracture (segmental) and for the said injury the petitioner has undergone surgery.
As per Ex.P.6 and 7 discharge summaries
, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 13 days, from 24-05-2024 to 05-06-2024 in PES Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Hospital, Kuppam.

In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injury sustained and the disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
24. Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.6 and 7 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 13 days in PES Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Hospital, Kuppam.

Vizalampura Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, the accident has taken place near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh and she has taken treatment at PES Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Hospital, Kuppam.

The petitioner has taken treatment for 13 days as in-patient at PES Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Hospital, Kuppam, for the grievous injuries sustained by her.

28. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 21 years and unfortunately she has sustained right proximal third tibial shaft fracture (segmental).
The evidence shows that, she has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 12% to the whole body.

Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/-
towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
29. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, united fracture proximal third (segmental) right tibia with implants in situ.
But, nowhere in the evidence the P.W.2 has stated that, the petitioner is in need of any further treatment.
In such circumstances, question of awarding compensation to the petitioner towards future medical expenses does not arise.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under the head future medical expenses.

30. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 4,27,680-00 2.

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,99,198/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
31. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MJ-1468.
The insurance policy bearing No.0516033123P116864129, issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending Tata Sumo bearing No.KA-01-MJ-1468, was valid from 17-03-2024 to 16-03-2025.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 24-05-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1/insured.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,99,198/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization,
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3
: In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,99,198/- (Rupees five lakh ninty nine thousand one hundred and ninty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment, on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner got stuck inside the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries.
Earlier to the accident she was working as tailor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity.
The Ramakuppam Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tata Sumo for the offence punishable under Section 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA SUMO bearing Reg.

17. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, she has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 24-05-2024 at about 11.45 p.m., near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, it is not the case of the respondent No.2 that, the accident has taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MJ-1468 involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.5 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MJ-1468 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468.
In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160442603/
5 of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 12% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove her avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
She has not produced any document to show that, before accident she was working as tailor and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,98,000/-.

30. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 4,27,680-00 2.
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,99,198/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore,
the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,99,198/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization,
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3
: In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,99,198/- (Rupees five lakh ninty nine thousand one hundred and ninty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment, on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
